messages.body_plain:
Hi, I am trying to use GGIR to perform a sleep analysis on a CWA-file from 14 days of measurements with the Axivity unit.

I am having trouble getting the id stored in part 2 to match that derived from the sleeplog csv-file and therefore get an error message when running part 4, resulting in no output from part 5.

Here is a breakdown of what I have tried:

1) First I tried using idloc=1 to prompt GGRI to extract the header information on id from the CWA-file. However, in the file part2_summary.csv I could see that no such information was extracted.

2) Then I tried using idloc=2 to prompt GGRI to extract the id from the the first part (before the underscore) of the filename of the CWA-file. This does indeed store a value for id in the file part2_summary.csv, in my case the value 32141, which corresponds to the first column value in my sleeplog, which is also 32141.

Now I expected all to be well. However, GGIR gave the following error message in part 4:

Part 4
 1
Warning: sleeplog id is stored as format: 32141, while
                           code expects format: 32
and later in part 5:

Report part 4
 loading all the milestone data from part 4 this can take a few minutes
Error in g.report.part4(datadir = datadir, metadatadir = metadatadir,  :
  object 'personSummarynames_backup' not found

Can anybody explain why this is happening? - and possibly a solution?

Best regards, Morten

P.S. I have attached my sleeplog.csv file and the part2_summary.csv file from step 2. Below is the GGIR script I am using:

library(GGIR)
g.shell.GGIR(#=======================================
             # INPUT NEEDED:
             mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
             datadir=  "E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/GGIR analyser/2019-04-08 - Test med 4 ure/32141-0000000011/Axivity data (CWA)",
             outputdir="E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/GGIR analyser/2019-04-08 - Test med 4 ure/32141-0000000011",
             f0=1, f1=c(),
             idloc=2, # id number drawn from: 1=file header, 2=numbers before the underscore in the filename
             desiredtz="Europe/Copenhagen",
             overwrite=TRUE, #overwrites previously created milestone data
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 1:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: reading file, auto-calibration, and extracting features
             do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,                printsummary=TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 1,               ndayswindow=7,
             hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
             maxdur = 9,                 includedaycrit = 16,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
             mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
             bout.metric = 4,
             closedbout=FALSE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Sleep detection
             timethreshold= c(5),        anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Integrating sleep log (if available) with sleep detection
             # storing day and person specific summaries of sleep
             excludefirstlast = TRUE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= "E:/Projekter/Axivity - Sleep/GGIR analyser/2019-04-08 - Test med 4 ure/32141-0000000011/sleeplog.csv",
             outliers.only = TRUE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = TRUE,
             sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = 14,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             #-------------------------------
             threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
             boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1),   timewindow = c("WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Generating reports based on meta-data
             do.report=c(2,4,5),
             visualreport=TRUE,     dofirstpage = TRUE,
             viewingwindow=1)

>
> I am currently analysing 24-h dataset for my research project and I wonder if anyone could share your thoughts of which output variables from Part 5 SUMMARY file should be included to get a 24h distribution among all behaviours (sleep, sedentary behaviour and PA)?
> Below are those variables which I think representative of the 24-hr analysis:
>
> sleep duration = dur_nightsleep_min
> sedentary time = dur_TINday_mi
> LPA time = dur_TLIGday_min

messages.body_plain:
HI all,

I recently fixed a bug related to idloc=2 in the development version
of GGIR on GitHub and will include this fix in the next release of
GGIR soon.
Possibly this will address your problem.

More detail about the bug that was fixed:
Using idloc=2 will make that GGIR looks for the ID in the filenmae as
whatever is before the first underscore of the name. However, the code
also automatically excludes the last character of it assuming that
this is a letter as was the case in one of the datasets I worked with.
I realise I never documented this well, hence the confusion also other
users experienced recently.

I have now adapted the code to first check whether the last character
is truly a letter and only exclude the letter if this is the case.

If you want to test this fix immediately then you can work with the
development version of GGIR via the following commands:

install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools)
install_github("wadpac/GGIR")

Do not forget to restart R/Rstudio after installing the package.
Best regards,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Errors when loading part 4
messages.body_plain:
Hi Anna,
Probably the error you get relates to trying to use a sleeplog datafile (csv).
What value for argument loglocation do you use?
If you omit it or set it to c() then GGIR will try to estimate sleep
without the sleeplog, which should avoid the error. Note that with
argument sleep.def.noc you can control how GGIR should do this, but
you can leave that to it's default setting if you are just starting.
If you want to GGIR to guide the sleep estimates with the sleeplog
file then it may help to first get the sleeplog to work with GGIR
function g.loadlog. If it does not work then that hints at incorrect
format/structure of the csv file. When the output of that looks
correct it should also work when integrated in GGIR.

If the problem persists then please share a bit more detail about your
situation: Number of nights in the data file, GGIR version number, and
also it would help if you could establish whether it is a file
specific problem or a consistent problem in all your files. Sharing a
milestone files produced by part3 and the sleeplog csv-file will ease
helping you.
Vincent

messages.subject: News update
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Version 1.9-1
I uploaded GGIR version 1.9-1 to CRAN yesterday, it may take a few days before it is available on MacOS and Windows. This release has only a few <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/news.html> minor bug fixes not relevant to most of you, but as the last release has already been two months ago it seemed good to create a new release. Additionally, I spent a couple of hours yesterday trying to improve the vignette <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html>. A couple of users recently indicated to me that the high number of optional arguments to function g.shell.GGIR can be overwhelming and that more guidance on it would be welcome. So, I especially worked on the section related to g.shell.GGIR. I imagine this can be improved further, but hopefully this is already a step forward relative to how it was. Feedback on how we can improve this further is definitely welcome.

GGIR overview paper accepted
A GGIR overview paper has been accepted in the Journal for the Measurement of Physical Behaviour with Jairo Migueles as first author. We hope this paper will provide an easy introduction to GGIR for new users and simplify citing GGIR in academic literature. Once it is online, we will incorporate a link to the paper in the GGIR documentation.

Consultancy service
As of this month I am full time independent consultant, available to provide consultancies related to wearable movement sensor data in the form of advise, training, or the development of methods and software.You can see this as a complementary service to the open source nature of GGIR. Altruistic community efforts to improve GGIR and to help new users are always welcome, but if you have a need for more dedicated time investments from me then this is now possible. Also, if you simply want to support me in leading and coordinating the maintenance of GGIR then the support service I launched last year is still ongoing https://movementdata.nl/how-to-help-sustain-ggir. At the moment my hourly price is 160 Euros (excluding service tax) for short consultancies lasting under two days. For longer consultancies I can offer reductions tailored to the duration and the type of service you require. Please get in touch for more information or see www.movementdata.nl <http://www.movementdata.nl>.

Meet the team
- At the end of June the ICAMPAM conference <https://ismpb.org/icampam/> will be held in Maastricht in The Netherlands. Jairo and I will both be there, and look forward meeting you there. Registration for the conference is still open.
- On the 6th of June I will be speaking in Oxford about GGIR at this <http://www.education.ox.ac.uk/events/earli-efg-physical-activity-and-rest-conference/> symposium "Physical activity and rest". Note: registration deadline is on the 29th of May.

GGIR used for sleep analysis in UKBiobank
In the past 5 months a series of high profile papers were published relating to GGIR's use for sleep analysis in UK Biobank https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-09576-1, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-018-08259-7, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-019-0361-7, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-08917-4 . This has received a lot of media attention and is helping to grow the GGIR user community. Special thanks to the team in Exeter (Samuel Jones, Andy Wood, Michael Weedon, Tim Frayling) for leading on this and obtaining the MRC grant that paid for 6 months of my time to develop the method to detect the sleep period time window underlying all this work.

Best wishes,
Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] ACC_nightandday_mg_wei vs ENMO_fullRecordingMean
messages.body_plain:
ACC_nightandday_mg_wei from part 5 is the weighted average of daily averages, where weighted refers to balancing weekend and weekdays following ration 5:2 (typical week)
ENMO_fullRecordingMean from part 2 is the average day using all available data in the recording minus invalid data (monitor not worn) by first taking the average per time section of the day and then the average of those averages. This allows for handling unbalanced availability of data throughout the 24-cycle while still using all the available data in a recording.

There is no hard evidence (yet) that one is better than the other, I would use the second one (part 2) if measurements are short and/or have a lot of missing data. In all other cases I would use the first one (part5) because it is probably easier to interpret, and it accounts for the weekend/weekday ratio, which the second one (part2) does not do.
Cheers, Vincent

I am using GGIR (ver. 1.9.1) on Axivity Ax3 data to measure sleep, but I am experiencing a problem in the g.part.3 inactivity bouts detection and, possibly, already in g.part.2.
The problem consists in inactivity bouts not corresponding to participant activity, as shown in the example below:

Here, the g.part3 meta output (sib.cla.sum, attached to this message) shows the first two inactivity bouts respectively from 01:05:05 to 01:14:55 and from 02:30:35 to 02:47:30. However, as you can see, there is  (1) no reason to end the first bout at 01:15 because the arm angle does not change, (2) no reason to start the second bout only at 02:30, since there are no evident movements meanwhile, and (3) it is not clear why the second bout ends only at 2:47 despite a clear movement at 02:40:46. This is the raw Ax3 recording:

I believe that the problem orignins already in g.part2, where intervals of stable arm angle (*) are classified as vigorous activity and it is not clear why only few inactivity intervals are considered as sleep/rest. Here you can see the g.part2 file summary report:
